name: Containers on AWS: ECS, EKS, ECR and Fargate

lesson.summary: A container packages an application together with everything it needs to run, so it behaves the same on any machine. Containers share the host operating system, which makes them lighter and faster to start than virtual machines. AWS offers tools for each part of the container job: Amazon ECR stores container images, Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS orchestrate containers across a fleet, and AWS Fargate runs containers without you managing the servers underneath.
keyPoints: A container packages an application with the libraries and settings it needs, so it runs the same on any compatible system
Containers share the host operating system, so they start faster and use fewer resources than virtual machines
Amazon ECR stores, manages and version controls container images
Amazon ECS orchestrates containers on AWS to deploy, scale and manage them
Amazon EKS runs Kubernetes, a popular open-source container orchestration system, as a managed service
AWS Fargate is a serverless compute option for containers, so you do not provision or manage the servers
ECS and EKS can run on EC2 instances you manage or on Fargate

scenarios.text: An e-commerce team builds a website that works on each developer's laptop but fails on the staging server because of missing libraries and different settings. The team wants the same application to run identically in every environment.

questions.prompt: Which approach best solves the problem in this scenario?

options.text: Package the application and its dependencies into a container image
Give each environment a different copy of the application code
Ask each developer to configure a separate laptop by hand
Move the website to a single virtual machine and stop testing

questions.explanation: A container packages the application with everything it needs, so the same image behaves the same in every environment. Separate copies, hand configuration and skipping testing do not give a consistent result.

questions.prompt: Match each AWS container service with what it does.

pairs.right: Runs containers without you managing servers

questions.explanation: ECS orchestrates containers, EKS runs Kubernetes as a managed service, ECR stores container images, and Fargate runs containers serverlessly.

questions.prompt: Which TWO statements about containers compared with virtual machines are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Containers do not include their own full operating system; virtual machine images do
Each container always runs its own full guest operating system
Container images are usually much smaller than virtual machine images

questions.explanation: Virtual machine images contain their own operating system and are much larger, while containers package only what one application needs. Containers cannot be run on AWS is false: AWS runs containers in several services.

questions.statement: With AWS Fargate you must provision and manage the EC2 servers that run your containers.
questions.explanation: False. Fargate is serverless compute for containers, so you do not provision or manage the servers underneath.

questions.prompt: Type the name of the AWS service where you store and manage container images.
questions.explanation: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (ECR) stores, manages and version controls container images.
